questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that the university offered courses within security and risk management, that it was a nice city to live in, and that the weather was nice most of the time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sydney is an amazing city to live in, and Macquarie University offers some really interesting and unique courses within security studies!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. It was a bit difficult to figure out how to register for courses. The course registration process was a bit complex, when registering for courses at master level, because you need to apply for a special approval for each course in order to enrol in a master level course at Macquarie University. In the special approval, you need to explain/argue how you live up to the necessary requirements for taking the course, which involve uploading the syllabus for previous classes you have taken. Information about this process was quit difficult to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation week hosted by Macquarie University the week before classes started, where you were able to sign up for different activities. This included a welcome meeting, where all relevant information was given and you could meet all the other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Information about how to register for courses and how the special approval process worked was very limited and could be improved. The orientation week was nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was quit lucky and found housing during the first week, when I arrived. But for some of the other exchange students, it was a bit more difficult to find housing. I would recommend to book a hostel or an airbnb for the two first weeks when you arrive to Sydney. Then you have time to find a place to live, explore the different neighbourhoods, and show up to open houses (which is often mandatory that you can show up to physically in order to get the place). I can recommend looking for places to rent on
www.domain.com.au
.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend to live off campus in the city of Sydney. It takes about 40 minutes/1 hour to get to campus from the city centre, but it is worth it! There is not much happening in the suburb where the campus is, so you get to explore Sydney more if you live off campus. I can recommend looking for places around Surry Hills, Darlinghurst, Kings Cross, Woolloomooloo, and Bondi (these areas are very trendy and cool, but also more expensive - but it is often even more expensive to live on-campus).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not know how easy it was to get housing through the university, as I did not look into this option.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was good and easy to understand.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to upload some different documents, including your grade transcripts, bachelor degree transcript (if you are applying for master), and proof of English proficiency. My proof of English proficiency was that my master and bachelor degree were in English. When you are accepted you receive a letter of confirmation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A contact email and phone number were provided, which you could write/ring to if you had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As mentioned the class registration process was quit complicated (at least when registering for master classes). In order to register for courses, you first need to apply for a special approval for each course in order to enrol in a master level course at Macquarie University. In the special approval, you need to explain/argue how you live up to the mandatory academic requirements for taking the course, which involve uploading the syllabus for previous relevant classes you have taken. Information about this process was quit difficult to find. But you can write to the contact email provided, and they will help you, or you can do some comprehensive researching and find the information on their website.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to apply for the special approvals as soon as the course registration opens to ensure that the application is processed before the semester starts. It can take weeks before the application is processed. Therefore, apply for more special approvals than you need, if some of your applications are rejected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Security Studies department at Macquarie University is great, as they offer some really interesting courses. However, many of the courses are scheduled to the same time, and it is therefore limited how many courses you can choose from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had four master level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Each course often consist of 1 hour of lecture, which is either in class or prerecorded so you can watch them online, and the followed by two hours of seminar. The seminars are generally quit small, around 20 people, where you are expected to participate and engage in the discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POIR8430: The Middle East in Global Politics, 
PICT8061: Transnational Security, 
PICT8018: Counter Terrorism in the Global and Australian Contexts, 
PICT8037: Choosing Terror - Pathways into Terrorism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would in particular recommend Counter Terrorism in the Global and Australian Contexts and Transnational Security. 
Counter Terrorism in the Global and Australian Contexts is a very relevant course in particular in today's world, and the course touches upon many different dilemmas and ways to counter terrorism and extremism. 
Transnational Security is likewise a very relevant and interesting course, touching upon different transnational security threats. The professor is also very sweet and talented.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I opened an Australian bank account to avoid paying fees every time I used my credit card. I can totally recommend that BUT be aware when you transfer money from your Danish bank account to your Australian bank account, because the exchange rate is often much worse. When making an international money transfer from your Danish bank account to your Australian, make sure that it is in AUS dollar and not in Danish kroner, then the exchange rate is better. Otherwise, you can end up loosing a lot of money due to the bad exchange rate that the Australian banks have.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in the supermarkets is generally more expensive than in Denmark. However, it is cheaper to eat at restaurants, cafes and takeaway. As a student at Macquarie University, you get a Student Opal card, which is a transport card that allows you to travel by public transport at half price! This makes public transport very cheap! The electricity bills in Sydney are also more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great. There are plenty of clubs and sports that you can join either for free or at a cheap price.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offered a very broad range of sports and social activities. The university also has a gym and a swimming pool, where you pay a weekly fee.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports team! It is a fun way to meet other students - both exchange students and local Australians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Sydney and go on weekend trips around NSW. Sydney has so many activities to offer and day trips that you can do, such as going to Manly, Bondi and Palm Beach. I would also recommend going to Royal National Park, where you can do different hikes, and it only takes about an hour by train. Hunter Valley is also lovely for a weekend trip, visiting vineyards. In September, you have a two week Spring break, which is the perfect opportunity to explore the rest of Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The Australian culture is very similar to the Danish, and people are very nice and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports team or social club at the University, and chat with people in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I do not really think that there were any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their appreciation for the beach and being outdoors.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Find a place to live in the city rather than on-campus, 2) Remember that you have two weeks of Spring break in September, where you can travel and explore Australia 3) Join a sports team or a social club

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Sydney is an expensive city to live in. I would recommend to apply for grants/scholarships - you can find an overview of all of them on
legatbogen.dk
. But remember to start applying for grants/scholarships early, as many of them have deadline 5-6 months before your exchange semester starts.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and living in Sydney for a semester, getting to explore Sydney's many amazing places and activities that it has to offer.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Hmmm, I am not sure. Maybe registering for courses?

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun! Sydney is amazing!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
